definitions.explanation: A sensation of cold, or the state of being cold, especially in the body.
A condition where parts of the body, especially hands and feet, feel persistently cold due to poor blood circulation.

examples.japanese: {朝晩|あさばん}の{冷|ひ}えに{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please be careful of the morning and evening chill.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{冷|ひ}えが{体|からだ}にこたえるようになる。
examples.english: When autumn comes, the chill starts to take its toll on the body.

examples.japanese: {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}で{困|こま}っている。
{手足|てあし}の{冷|ひ}えがひどい。
examples.english: The coldness in my hands and feet is severe.

examples.japanese: {冷|ひ}えを{改善|かいぜん}するために{毎日|まいにち}{半身浴|はんしんよく}をしている。
examples.english: I take a half-body bath every day to improve my cold sensitivity.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {冷|ひ}える (to get cold). Refers both to ambient chill and to the common health complaint of poor circulation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷|ひ}え{性|しょう} — sensitivity to cold, poor circulation
- {手足|てあし}の{冷|ひ}え — cold hands and feet
- {冷|ひ}え{対策|たいさく} — measures against cold/poor circulation
- {冷|ひ}えを{防|ふせ}ぐ — to prevent chilling
- {冷|ひ}え{込|こ}み — sharp drop in temperature

HEALTH CONTEXT:
{冷|ひ}え{性|しょう} is a commonly discussed health condition in Japan, particularly among women. It is considered a cause of various ailments in traditional Japanese and Chinese medicine. Remedies include warm baths, ginger tea, and layered clothing.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寒|さむ}さ — coldness (of weather or environment)
- {冷|つめ}たさ — coldness (of objects or attitude)
